Ukrainian F-16 Shoots Down Russian Su-35 in First Aerial Kill, US General Says — The senior US general told the Senate that a Ukrainian F-16 shot down a Russian Su-35 in a recent engagement, marking the first known F-16-versus-Su-35 air combat victory. The Su-35 forms the backbone of Russia’s fighter fleet and has been exported to several countries, including Iran.

Russia's Su-57 Fifth-Generation Fighter Jet Crashes Near Moscow — A Russian Su-57 fifth-generation fighter jet crashed during a training flight near Moscow. The pilot ejected safely, no casualties were reported, and Russian authorities have not yet disclosed the cause of the incident.

Russia Warns US Against Ukraine Arms Sales as Top Diplomats Meet in Manila — Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told US Secretary of State Marco Rubio that further American arms deliveries to Ukraine were “unacceptable” during talks in Manila, while urging a diplomatic solution. The meeting came as Kyiv seeks to revive peace efforts and Washington shifts focus back to ending the war.

Irish PM Visits Kyiv as Ireland Makes Ukraine Top EU Presidency Priority — Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin arrived in Kyiv for talks with President Volodymyr Zelensky, pledging Ireland will make support for Ukraine and its EU membership bid a top priority during its six-month presidency of the Council of the EU.

EU Agrees on 21st Russia Sanctions Package — EU ambassadors have agreed on the bloc’s 21st sanctions package against Russia after weeks of disputes over measures targeting Moscow. The deal follows objections from several member states that forced Brussels to scale back some proposals, but the package will still expand economic pressure on the Kremlin.

Russia Restricts Nighttime Shipping at its Largest Cargo Port After Ukrainian Drone Attacks — Russia has reportedly imposed nighttime restrictions at Novorossiysk, its largest cargo port, as Ukrainian attacks disrupt Black Sea shipping. The measures, alongside disruptions on Ukraine’s coast, have tightened grain export routes and pushed wheat prices higher.

Kremlin Prepares for Mobilization as Putin Downplays Deepening Fuel Crisis — ISW says Russia is preparing legal and security measures for possible mobilization while bracing for domestic unrest. Despite worsening fuel shortages and mounting economic pressure, Putin insists the economy remains stable and resilient.

223-Drone Raid Hits Russian Regions, Sparking Fires at Oil and Energy Facilities — Ukraine reportedly struck a Wildberries logistics hub, an oil refinery, and a major oil pipeline station during overnight drone attacks. Russia said it intercepted 223 drones while acknowledging casualties and damage across several regions.

Explosions Rock Occupied Crimea as Drones Reportedly Target Sevastopol and Yalta — The latest reported drone attack on occupied Crimea focused on military and energy-related infrastructure, including positions near Sevastopol and sites in Yalta.

Ukraine Calls Emergency UN Meeting as Russian Strikes Halt Black Sea Shipping — Kyiv has called for an urgent UN Security Council meeting after Russian attacks disrupted civilian shipping and further strained Ukraine’s Black Sea grain exports.

Ukrainian Soldiers Welcome Drapaty as Army Chief but Still Want Fedorov Back — Ukrainian soldiers and civilians welcomed Mykhailo Drapaty’s appointment as army commander, while many continued to call for former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov to return to government.

Rubio, Lavrov to Hold First Face-to-Face Meeting Since September in Manila to Discuss Ukraine — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov are set for their first in-person meeting since September, with Ukraine at the center of discussions.

Zelensky Invited to Graham Funeral as Kyiv Plans Possible Trump Meeting — Ukraine is considering a late-July visit by President Volodymyr Zelensky to the US for Lindsey Graham’s funeral and a possible meeting with President Donald Trump.

Zelensky Speaks With Witkoff, Kushner on Advancing Ukraine Peace Talks — President Volodymyr Zelensky spoke with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner about intensifying diplomacy toward ending the Russian war, saying Ukraine has long been ready for peace and thanking US President Donald Trump for continued US support.

Angola Court Jails 2 Russian Spies on Espionage, Terrorism Charges — Angola has jailed two Russians for 11 and 8 years respectively under charges that range from espionage to terrorism. Authorities accused the two of paying locals over $24,000 to spread anti-Western and pro-Russian propaganda and staging deadly protests, but the two denied the charges by arguing they were merely in the country to establish a Russian cultural center.

Czech Ministries Draft Law to Let Companies, Police Down Stray Drones — The Czech Interior and Transport Ministries have drafted legislation allowing police and infrastructure operators to eliminate drones flying illegally near critical sites. The bill, now in interagency review, sets clear no-fly zones with defined intervention rules.

Belarus to Send Poorly Performing Farmers to Guard Ukraine Border — Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko said underperforming harvest workers – and officials – should be sent to the army to guard the Ukraine border as Minsk rallied for a bountiful harvest season. Despite the call, he said he has no intention to start a war with Ukraine, framing the order as a way to improve the workers’ general wellbeing.

Russian Strikes Wound 7 in Dnipropetrovsk Region — Russian armed forces attacked two districts of Ukraine’s Dnipropetrovsk region more than 40 times with drones, artillery, and an aerial bomb, wounding seven people and damaging infrastructure and homes.

Russia Expands Prison Recruitment for Ukraine War With New Bill — Russia’s State Duma passed a bill on Wednesday to broaden the pool of potential military recruits from among prisoners, with those serving a sentence for organized crime and mishandling state secrets also eligible for service amid recent reports that Moscow has failed to hit its recruitment targets despite higher financial incentives.

Hungary Blocks EU Clusters 2,3 for Ukraine, Moldova’s Accession Talks — Hungary refused to approve EU accession clusters 2 and 3 for the second time, scheduling the next attempt for Sept. 1. Budapest previously argued that opening all clusters at once wouldn’t be fair to other candidates in the Western Balkans.

Why Is Ukraine Attacking Wildberries? Here’s Why — Ukraine has destroyed several more warehouses belonging to Wildberries, one of Russia’s largest retail businesses. The attacks have dealt a serious blow to Russia’s small and medium-sized businesses. But what lies behind Ukraine’s strikes?

Zelensky Receives Washington’s NATO Envoy in Kyiv to Talk Air Defense, Drone Deal — President Volodymyr Zelensky said he discussed the Patriot’s transfers and licensed production in Kyiv with US Ambassador to NATO Matthew Whitaker and Lt. Gen. Curtis Buzzard, the commander of NATO Security Assistance & Training for Ukraine. Russia Moves to ‘Cancel’ Political Exiles With Asset Freezes — Rights lawyers call it the “de facto deprivation of citizenship,” while Moscow pressures them to return and “confess.”

Germany Approves Controversial French-Russian Nuclear Project — Germany has approved a Framatome-Rosatom project in Lingen to produce fuel rods for Russian-designed reactors, despite warnings it could expose sensitive nuclear infrastructure to spying and sabotage risks.

'Gasoline Situation Is F***ed' – Fuel Crisis Hits Russian Army as Troops Report Severe Shortages — Russian soldiers say fuel shortages caused by Ukraine's refinery strikes have led to rationing, disrupted logistics, and higher costs. Some troops report walking miles for supplies as volunteer groups also appeal for gasoline donations.

Ukraine’s New Military Commander Maj. Gen. Mykhailo Drapaty: 5 Things to Know — Mykhailo Drapaty, Ukraine’s new senior officer, is renowned for frontline leadership since 2014. He pioneered large-scale drone-centric warfare, helped liberate Kherson, and is respected for decentralized command, innovation, and accepting responsibility for battlefield failures.

UK, Germany Team Up on Secret Long-Range Missile to Strike Russia — Britain and Germany are developing a classified missile under the Deep Precision Strike program. The project aims to strengthen NATO's long-range strike capability while reducing Europe's reliance on US military systems.

Lavrov, Rubio to Meet in Manila as Kremlin Hardens Ukraine Position — Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov will meet US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Manila for their first face-to-face talks since September, as the Kremlin reportedly abandons the idea of a territorial swap with Ukraine and doubles down on plans to retain occupied border areas as a buffer zone.

Ukraine: Why Was Army Chief Syrskyi Fired? — President Volodymyr Zelensky replaced Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi with General Mykhailo Drapatyi after protests sparked by the dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. Commentators are divided: some see the move as a response to public pressure and a step toward military reform, while others praise Syrskyi’s wartime record or criticize Zelensky’s leadership style.

‘An Enormous Shitstorm Is Coming’: Russians React to Ukraine’s Wildberries Strikes — “Many people will wake up bankrupt,” one Russian seller said after another Wildberries warehouse went up in flames. A series of Ukrainian drone strikes has exposed fear, anger, and doubts about the Kremlin’s ability to protect Russia’s logistics network.

Ukraine's Drone Offensive Hits 13 Russian Ships and Crimea's Power Grid in 48 Hours — Ukraine says its drones struck 13 Russian vessels and 13 energy facilities over two days. The attacks are part of separate campaigns targeting Russia's maritime logistics and power infrastructure in occupied Crimea and other occupied territories.

Zelensky Appoints Major General Ihor Skybiuk as New Chief of Ukraine’s General Staff Amid Military Shake-Up — Volodymyr Zelensky has appointed Major General Ihor Skybiuk as the new Chief of Ukraine’s General Staff, completing a major military leadership reshuffle that also saw Mykhailo Drapaty named the new AFU commander-in-chief.

Kremlin Rules Out Returning Occupied Sumy, Kharkiv Border Areas in Peace Deal – Bloomberg — Russia no longer plans to return occupied parts of Ukraine’s Sumy and Kharkiv regions in any future peace deal, according to Bloomberg. The Kremlin reportedly intends to keep the border areas as buffer zones while pressing ahead with its goal of capturing the entire Donetsk and Luhansk regions.

Lithuania Moves Red Army Graves to Leave Behind Soviet Past — Lithuania is exhuming Soviet Red Army graves as part of its drive to erase symbols of Soviet occupation, drawing sharp protests from Moscow. The wartime memorial relocations have become the latest flashpoint in a broader battle over history, memory, and Russia’s influence in the Baltic region.

EU’s New Russia Sanctions Stall as Member States Defend Own Interests — The EU is pushing to approve its 21st Russia sanctions package, but internal disputes over LNG, shipping, banking and trade have forced major compromises. Despite Viktor Orbán’s departure from Hungary’s leadership, member states are still struggling to agree on how far to go in pressuring Moscow.

Putin’s AI Army: Deepfakes Posing as Polish Soldiers Spread Kremlin Lies About Ukraine — Polish authorities say Kremlin-linked actors used AI-generated videos posing as Polish soldiers to spread anti-Ukrainian narratives. Cybersecurity experts identified Russian-language traces and other manipulation, while several accounts were later removed.

Syrsky Says Army Went From Defense to Offensive Before Exit as Russia Declares Drapatyi Wanted — Outgoing AFU chief Syrsky defended his wartime leadership, highlighting battlefield gains and military reforms. Meanwhile, Russia placed newly appointed Commander-in-Chief Drapatyi on its wanted list without specifying the charges.

Ukraine Strikes 2 Major Logistics Hubs of Russia’s Largest Online Retailer — Ukrainian drones struck two of Wildberries' largest logistics centers in southern Russia, injuring several people and hitting an oil depot. The attack follows previous strikes on the retailer's distribution network.

Fedorov welcomed the move as “a breath of fresh air and new hope,” while Zelensky offered him a new technology-focused government role.

Inside Dnipro Hospital Where Russian Drone Wounds Have Replaced Bullet Injuries — Dnipro’s central hospital has become a key treatment center for soldiers and civilians wounded across eastern and southern Ukraine. Doctors say the nature of injuries has changed since Russia’s full-scale invasion, with bullet wounds increasingly replaced by devastating trauma from drones, missiles and glide bombs.

US Senate Places Ukraine Aid Bill on Calendar — The US Senate has completed the Rule 14 process for H.R. 2913, the Ukraine Support Act, placing the House-passed bill directly on the Senate Calendar of Business. The procedural move bypasses traditional committee review and allows Senate leadership to bring the measure to the floor, though it does not guarantee a vote. The bill includes military support, reconstruction aid and expanded Russia sanctions.

UN Says Civilian Casualties in Ukraine War Rose 37 Percent in First Half of 2026 — Civilian casualties in Russia’s war against Ukraine rose by 37 percent in the first half of 2026, AFP reported, citing the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine. Danielle Bell said monitors documented 1,396 civilians killed and 7,978 injured, with long-range ballistic missiles, drones, glide bombs and FPV drones driving the increase.

Speaking alongside German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Berlin, Aliyev said Azerbaijan was not officially informed by either side. Fedorov Responds to Syrsky's Dismissal, Calls Drapaty 'New Hope' — Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov congratulated newly appointed Commander-in-Chief Mykhailo Drapaty, calling his selection “a voice of change that could not be ignored.” Fedorov, whose dismissal sparked mass protests last week, had previously pushed for Syrsky’s removal.

Zelensky Offered Fedorov a New Position. Did Not Specify Which One — Volodymyr Zelensky offered a new position to former Minister of Defense Mykhailo Fedorov after six days of mass protests in his support. However, the president did not specify what the position would be.

Syrsky Dismissed as Commander-in-Chief, Drapaty Replaces Him — President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Maj. Gen. Mykhailo Drapatyi will become Ukraine’s new commander-in-chief, replacing Oleksandr Syrsky. The move follows days of protests and speculation over a shake-up in the country’s military leadership.

Ukrainian MP Zhelezniak Hints Drapaty May Replace Syrsky — Yaroslav Zhelezniak, first deputy chair of Ukraine’s parliament, Verkhovna Rada’s finance committee, signaled possible military shakeup tomorrow, hinting that Mykhailo Drapaty, the commander of Ukraine’s Joint Forces Command might be Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Oleksandr Syrsky replacing amid a deepening crisis in the country’s defense leadership.

Ukraine Completes Formation of Regional Youth Congresses — Ukraine finished forming regional youth congresses in all its regions on Tuesday, electing leaders and delegates under a structure created by President Volodymyr Zelensky. The move adds 1,469 new representatives and 300 delegates to the National Congress.

5 Wounded as Russia Strikes Dnipropetrovsk Region — Russian armed forces attacked two districts of Ukraine’s Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 40 times with drones and artillery on Tuesday, wounding five people. A 65-year-old man remains in critical condition after strikes hit residential and commercial buildings.

The Battle Beyond the Battlefield: Winning Back Hearts — Ukraine’s wartime image in the West, once bolstered by its heroic resistance, is eroding — partly due to a historical dispute with Poland over the UPA’s legacy. After Zelensky named a unit after UPA figures tied to WWII massacres of Poles, tensions flared. The piece argues Ukraine needs pragmatic, durable solutions on historical memory, not nationalist rhetoric, to protect its EU membership prospects.

EU Agency Halts Venice Biennale Funding Over Russia’s Return — The EU's education and culture agency has terminated a €2 million (roughly $2.2 million) grant to the Venice Biennale after organizers allowed Russia's pavilion to reopen. Ukraine and more than twenty European countries had pushed for Russia's exclusion.

Secret Baku Talks Confirmed Between German and Russian Officials — Azerbaijani President confirmed that former German and Russian officials secretly met in Baku on July 12–14 to discuss Russia's war against Ukraine. However, German Chancellor said his government had no involvement and was unaware of the meeting taking place.

Black Sea Naval War Heats Up as Russia, Ukraine Trade Fiery Attacks vs Civilian Ships — Ukraine and Russia have escalated Black Sea attacks on civilian shipping. Ukrainian drones struck tankers at Russia’s KTK terminal, while Russian missiles hit the grain ship Golden Leo, killing 10 in likely the war’s deadliest attack on a merchant vessel.

Gas Tanker En Route to Ukraine Struck Off Romanian Coast in Potential Russian Strike — Romania’s president said the Liberia-flagged LPG tanker Gas Lisbon was struck in Romanian waters late Monday, injuring three crew members. Romania and Ukraine blamed Russia for the attack, the latest in a string of strikes on vessels as both Kyiv and Moscow have intensified strikes in the Black Sea.

Ukraine Hits Russian MiG-29, Pantsir System at Kursk Airfield in $45M Blow — Ukraine says its forces hit a Russian MiG-29 fighter jet and a Pantsir-S1 air defense system at the Khalino airfield in Russia’s Kursk region. Drone footage released by the military appears to show the operation, though its authenticity has not been independently verified.

Russia Adds More Rassvet Satellites, Attempting to Build Its Own ‘Starlink’ — Russia has launched a second batch of Rassvet satellites, increasing its Starlink-like constellation to about 40 orbiters. Analysts say the network remains far from military readiness, as Moscow will need several hundred satellites before it can provide reliable battlespace C3.

Waiting for AFU Chief’s Dismissal: Who Could Replace Him? — As protests in Kyiv increasingly target Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrsky, opinion within the military is divided, with some backing calls for change while others argue that replacing the army’s leadership during wartime would be a dangerous mistake. Meanwhile, President Volodymyr Zelensky is reportedly meeting with six senior commanders who are viewed as potential successors, though no decision on Syrsky’s future has been made.

Russian Warship Conducts Live-Fire Drill Off Britain’s Plymouth — The Russian frigate Neustrashimy conducted a 30-minute live-fire exercise in international waters about 40 nautical miles off the British coastal city of Plymouth on Monday. The drill coincided with the appointment of Britain’s new prime minister and followed a string of incidents involving Russian vessels near British waters.

Crimea Plunges Into Darkness Again as Fresh Blasts Hit Russian Energy Grid — New explosions struck occupied Crimea overnight, damaging key power substations and triggering fresh blackouts. As Ukraine’s campaign against Russian energy infrastructure intensifies, occupation authorities are installing emergency street telephones and struggling to maintain basic services.

Ukraine’s New Drones Turn Russian Supply Routes Into Hunting Grounds — Ukraine’s new mid-range strike drones are opening a new battlespace behind Russian lines, targeting supply routes once considered safe. The drones are disrupting logistics, expanding Ukraine’s geographic attack envelope and forcing Russia to defend a growing number of vulnerable areas.

Pro-Trump Influencer Laura Loomer Visits Ukraine, Changes Tone on Russia — Laura Loomer, a pro-Trump influencer and former Ukraine critic, has visited Ukraine and apologized for her previous pro-Kremlin rhetoric, saying she was a victim of Russian propaganda as she began to hit back at Kremlin messaging during the past few months.

For Ukraine’s Drones, Names Are Part of the Battle — Ukrainian drone makers are turning dark humour into a weapon, giving their systems names that mock Russia and boost morale. From the “Pissioun” interceptor to the “Liutyi” strike drone, the names have become symbols of resistance as Kyiv expands its drone war.

Fire Erupts Near Russia’s Largest Steel Plant After Reported Drone Attack in Lipetsk — A fire broke out near Russia’s largest steel producer, Novolipetsk Steel, in Lipetsk after residents reported explosions and a possible drone attack overnight. Russian officials confirmed a fire at industrial facilities but did not acknowledge an attack, while Ukraine has not commented.

Gen. Mykhailo Drapaty amid a deepening crisis in the country’s defense leadership. The reported discussions come after the dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov triggered the largest protests of Zelensky’s presidency.

IMF Approves $690 million for War-Torn Ukraine After Review — The International Monetary Fund’s board completed a review of Ukraine’s financing arrangement, clearing the way for immediate access to about $690 million, the Fund said on Monday.

Former SBU Special Forces Chief Takes Over Ukraine’s Defense Ministry Amid Fedorov Fallout — Former SBU Special Forces chief Yevhen Khmara took over as Ukraine’s acting defense minister on July 20 following President Volodymyr Zelensky’s decision to appoint him to the role. The move comes as protests continue over the dismissal of reformist Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov.

Sanctioning Russia is Popular in America — A bipartisan survey shows overwhelming US support for tougher measures against Russia, with strong backing for sanctions, actions against officials involved in abducting Ukrainian children, and penalties on foreign companies doing business with Moscow. Majorities across Republicans, Democrats, and independents also favor expanding US–Ukraine defense cooperation.

Zelensky Faces Deepening Political Crisis as Protests Dig In — President Volodymyr Zelensky faces mounting political pressure as protests over the dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov enter a fifth day. Demonstrators demand military reforms and the removal of Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrsky, while the government weighs changes to avoid deepening divisions during the war.

Crimea Installs Landline Payphones as Mobile Blackouts Persist — Russian occupation authorities in Crimea have begun installing public payphones after scheduled mobile network shutoffs and Ukrainian strikes left residents without communication. The devices reportedly work even without electricity and connect free of charge to emergency services.
